cues.en: Well, my daddy left home when I was three, and he didn't leave much. The more in me, just this old guitar and an empty bottle of food.
cues.zh: 嗯，我三岁时爸爸就离家出走，没留下多少东西。只留下这把旧吉他，还有一个空空的食物瓶。

cues.en: Now I don't blame him because he run and hid, but the meanest thing that he ever did was before he left, he went and named me Sue.
cues.zh: 我不怪他逃走躲起来，可他做过最过分的事，就是离开前给我取名叫 Sue。

cues.en: Well, I grew up quick and I grew up mean. My fist got hard, my wits got keen. Roam from town to town to hide my shame.
cues.zh: 我很快长大，也变得狠厉。拳头越来越硬，脑子也越来越灵光。我从一个小镇流浪到另一个小镇，只为藏起自己的羞耻。

cues.en: But I made me a vow to the moon and stars. I'd search the Humpy Thompson bars and kill that man who'd give me that awful name.
cues.zh: 可我对着月亮和星星发誓：我要找遍 Humpy Thompson 的酒吧，杀了那个给我起这难听名字的人。

cues.en: Well, it was Gatlinburg in mid July, and I just hit town and my throat was dry. I thought I'd stop and have myself a groove.
cues.zh: 那是在七月中旬的加特林堡，我刚进城，口渴得厉害，就想着歇歇脚找点乐子。

cues.en: At an old saloon on a street of mud, there at a table, dealing stud, such a dirty mangy dog that named me Sue.
cues.zh: 在泥泞街道旁的一家老酒馆里，坐在桌边发着梭哈牌的，正是那个给我起名叫 Sue 的下流邋遢狗。

cues.en: Well, I knew that snake was my own sweet dad from a worn out picture that my mother had had, and I knew that scar on his cheek and his evil eye.
cues.zh: 从我母亲留着的一张破旧照片上，我认出那个混蛋就是我的亲爹，我也认出了他脸上的伤疤和那副凶相。

cues.en: He was big and bent and gray and old, and I looked at him and my blood ran cold. I said, my name is Sue.
cues.zh: 他又高又驼，头发花白，老态龙钟，我看着他，顿时心头一凉，说道：“我叫 Sue。”

cues.en: How do you do?
cues.zh: 你好啊？

cues.en: And are you gonna die?
cues.zh: 你会死吗？

cues.en: Yeah. That's what I told him.
cues.zh: 是啊，我就是这么跟他说的。

cues.en: Well, I hit him hard right between the eyes, and he went down. But to my surprise,
cues.zh: 我一拳正中他眉心，他倒下了。但让我意外的是，

cues.en: he come up with a knife and cut off a piece of my ear.
cues.zh: 他爬起来掏出刀子，割掉了我一只耳朵。

cues.en: But I busted a chair right across his teeth, we crashed through the wall and into the street, kicking and a gouging in the mud and the blood and the beard.
cues.zh: 但我抡起椅子砸在他牙上，我们撞穿墙壁冲进街上，在泥里、血里、胡子里又踢又抠。

cues.en: I tell you, I fought tougher men, but I really can't remember when.
cues.zh: 跟你说，我打过更狠的，但真想不起来是什么时候了。

cues.en: He kicked like a mule and he bit like a crocodile.
cues.zh: 他踢起人来像骡子，咬起人来像鳄鱼。

cues.en: I heard him laugh, and then I heard him cuss, and he went for his gun to pull mine first. He stood there looking at me, and I saw him smile. He said, son,
cues.zh: 我听见他笑了，接着又听见他骂骂咧咧。他伸手去拿枪，想抢先拔出我的枪。他站在那里看着我，我看见他笑了。他说，孩子，

cues.en: this world is rough, and if a man's gonna make it, he's gotta be tough. And I know I wouldn't be there to help you along.
cues.zh: 这世道很艰难，一个男人要想闯出一片天，就得坚强。我知道我没法在你身边帮你走下去。

cues.en: So I give you that name, and I said goodbye, and you you'd have to get tough or die. And it's that name that helped to make you strong.
cues.zh: 所以我给你取了那个名字，然后跟你告别。你得变得坚强，否则就只能死去。正是这个名字让你变得强大。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 对。

cues.en: He said, now you just fought one hell of a fight, and I know you hate me, and you've got the right to kill me now, and I wouldn't blame you if you do.
cues.zh: 他说：“你刚才打得可真够狠的，我知道你恨我，你现在完全有理由杀了我，就算动手我也绝不怪你。

cues.en: But you ought to thank me before I die for the gravel in your guts and the spit in the eye, because I'm the son of a bitch that named you Sue.
cues.zh: 但在我死之前，你该谢谢我，是我让你骨子里有了狠劲、眼里有了杀气，因为老子就是那个给你起名叫 Sue 的混蛋。”

cues.en: Yeah. What could I do? What could I do?
cues.zh: 是啊，我还能怎么办？我能怎么办呢？

cues.en: I got all choked up and I threw down my gun, called him a paw, and he called me a son, and I come away with a different point of view.
cues.zh: 我哽咽了，扔掉了手里的枪，叫了他一声爹，他也叫了我一声儿子，离开时我的想法全变了。

cues.en: And I think about him now and then every time I try and every time I win.
cues.zh: 我时不时会想起他，每次我尝试时，每次我成功时。

cues.en: And if I ever have a son,
cues.zh: 如果我有个儿子，

cues.en: I think I'm gonna name him Bill or George, any damn thing but Sue.
cues.zh: 我想我会给他取名 Bill 或 George，什么都行，就是不要叫 Sue。

cues.en: I'm telling you this. Yeah.
cues.zh: 我跟你说这些。是啊。
